title: Forman & Kent 2011 costal cartilage instantaneous modulus from spherical indentation (rib 4)

quantity.name: instantaneous elastic modulus E0
quantity.definition: characteristic average instantaneous elastic modulus from linear viscoelastic fits of spherical indentation (2 mm sphere, 0.25 mm depth)

source.sample: 5 fourth-rib costal cartilage specimens (with sternal portion and ~3 cm rib, perichondrium removed) from 5 cadavers; 3-4 cross-sectional slices each, 14-20 indentation tests per specimen

protocol.summary: Cross-sectional slices (~6 mm thick) potted, soaked 30 min in physiologic saline at body temperature; spherical indentation (2 mm diameter tip) at ~0.5 mm/s to ~0.25 mm depth (~4% of thickness); linear viscoelastic (instantaneous modulus + relaxation function) fitted; characteristic average instantaneous modulus E0 per specimen.
how_to_simulate: Indent a costal cartilage cross-section with a 2 mm diameter rigid sphere at 0.5 mm/s to 0.25 mm
Fit or compare the instantaneous elastic modulus E0 (half-space Hertz with linear viscoelasticity)

data.x: specimen 403 rib 4L (47 y M; 4 slices, 20 tests)
specimen 322 rib 4L (49 y M; 4 slices, 19 tests)
specimen 400 rib 4L (53 y M; 3 slices, 14 tests)
specimen 187 rib 4R (54 y M; 4 slices, 16 tests)
specimen 197 rib 4R (57 y F; 3 slices, 14 tests)
